textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 10 social-science · Political Science 4: Political Parties · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: A political party is a group of people who come together to contest elections and hold power in government. They agree on policies for the good of society.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: A political party is a group of people who come together to contest elections and hold power in government. They agree on policies for the good of society.
beats.speakEn: A political party is a group of people who come together to contest elections and hold power in government. They agree on policies for the good of society.

beats.en: Parties contest elections, put forward policies and programmes, make laws, form and run governments, play the role of opposition, shape public opinion and run welfare schemes.
beats.speakEn: Parties contest elections, put forward policies and programmes, make laws, form and run governments, play the role of opposition, shape public opinion and run welfare schemes.

type: Key Concept: A political party is a group of people who come together to contest elections and hold power

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 10 social-science · Political Science 4: Political Parties · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: A party has leaders, active members and followers. Parties are necessary because democracy needs representation and competition.

beats.en: A party has leaders, active members and followers. Parties are necessary because democracy needs representation and competition.
beats.speakEn: A party has leaders, active members and followers. Parties are necessary because democracy needs representation and competition.

beats.en: In a one-party, two-party or multi-party system, the number of parties vary. India has a multi-party system with alliances.
beats.speakEn: In a one-party, two-party or multi-party system, the number of parties vary. India has a multi-party system with alliances.

type: A party has leaders, active members and followers.
In a one-party, two-party or multi-party system, the number of parties vary.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 10 social-science · Political Science 4: Political Parties · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: The Election Commission registers parties and recognises national parties. A national party must get at least six per cent of total votes in four states and win at least four seats in the Lok Sabha.

beats.en: Let us review the key takeaway from Political Science 4: Political Parties: The Election Commission registers parties and recognises national parties. A national party must get at least six per cent of total votes in four states and win at least four seats in the Lok Sabha.
